comparison.source: 20 min progressive + 3×30 s Z5 r60 s; main 5–7×3 min Z5 r3 min Z1–Z2; 10 min cool-down. The final rest policies remain unresolved in the original and candidate in V19.
comparison.studyPopulation: Narrative programming review with examples from several sports; no single intervention cohort or athlete-specific dose established.
comparison.studyProtocol: Review of work/relief intensity and duration, modality, repetitions, series and between-series recovery, plus cardiopulmonary and non-cardiopulmonary loads.
comparison.studyComparator: Programming configurations discussed in a narrative review, not a direct trial of this TFCL recipe.
comparison.studyResults: Work/recovery configuration can alter acute physiological responses; cardiorespiratory response alone does not capture all loading.
comparison.differences: No direct validation of 5–7×3 min, Z5 individual domain, 3-min recovery, final-rest occurrence, weekly frequency or VLamax-based restriction. Existing source restrictions remain unchanged.

comparison.source: 4×15 min Z2 en position aéro, r5 min Z1; unknown original final-rest occurrence; candidate totals 75 or 80 min. Source avoid: lumbar pain. The archived 6×10 alternative has another continuous exposure.
comparison.studyPopulation: 20 cyclists; results about perceptions across tested positions, not an individual Ironman cohort tolerance certificate.
comparison.studyProtocol: Three tests in randomized order, 45 min at 50% individual peak aerobic power, with different knee and trunk flexion combinations.
comparison.studyComparator: Different bicycle positions at the experimental workload, not 4×15 versus 6×10 min bouts.
comparison.studyResults: Perceptions of comfort, fatigue and pain varied across positions; upright trunk was more comfortable in the study's recreational context.
comparison.differences: Study intensity is relative to peak aerobic power, not automatically Z2/FTP. No 15-min bout tolerance, recovery duration, aerodynamic gain or equivalence of interruptions is demonstrated.
